method: Direct selected passages via web open; paraphrased observations only; no dictionary assets acquired.

consultations.observation: The selected rank/precedence sense is distinct from a countable important item. Neither selected passage showed CEFR. B2 remains an independent editorial placement, with all priority-policy domain holds unchanged.

Postal/location details can be spoken, so removing necessarily-written is supported. Collins selected postal A1 is literal; course A2 is a floor, not a source level. Computing/electronic addresses stay distinct.
Oxford selected topic B2 supports bounded scheduling placement. Collins shared-standard-time region supports the retained definition. Simplified 24-zone/one-hour-adjacency claims are not adopted.

Oxford selected authorization A2 and Collins selected B1 disagree. A2 is reasonable for the bounded schedule-change example. Electronic permissions and written permissions are separate senses; current ambiguity holds remain.
Oxford ordinary work-item A2 contrasts with Collins B2. Concrete welcome-pack work supports bounded A2; no difficulty/project requirement or operating-system sense is imported.

Oxford organizational position/function and Collins position/function B2 support the narrowed definition and B2 placement. Actor A2/B1+ labels are separate. A role is not proof of authority or professional competence.
Both selected response-to-work passages show B2. Evaluation/information broadens comments appropriately while excluding electrical and control feedback. Uncountability and one-word noun remain.
Oxford permits countable assigned duties, and Collins plural duties B2 supports the proposed example one of my responsibilities. Duty is not blame, legal liability or universal authority.
Selected general place supports an activity location. Oxford B1 and Collins literal B1+ remain separate from Collins exact-position B2. B1 is editorial, not a rounded Collins level.

The ordinary characteristic written-name noun supports the retained meaning and Collins B1 placement. A signing act, style, stamp, prescription or electronic authentication does not acquire acceptance.
